readings.task: Read the LINES (half-breadth) plan ends on drawing 11 (RG19_ALPHA_Constitution_1797_11.JPG): find the baseline and station ticks, fit px to work X, find the half-breadth scale, sample waterlines A-F plus the top lines at stations 10, 9.5, 9, 8, 2, 1, 0.5 and 0, find where each curve ends, get waterline heights from the sheer and body plans, and cross-check against source_lines.json d11 at stations 8 and 2.
readings.calibration: These are partial results; I went over the 20-minute budget. All six waterlines A-F are traced and checked against the letters on the drawing, so their stern and bow values and end points are solid (about ±1.5 px, or ±0.25 cells). The RAIL and SPAR DECK curves are only partly done: I have pixel positions for the top lines at stations 10, 2, 1 and 0.5, but I could not reliably tell which of them is RAIL and which is SPAR DECK. At station 2, waterlines A-D sit in a crowd of 5 lines near the top and their assignment is ambiguous. One important result: the half-breadths in the LINES plan run vertically on the sheet. Treating them with the vertical scale (19.25 px/ft) fits the body plan much better than the horizontal scale (18.5 px/ft) does, and even then the LINES values come out about 2% wider than source_lines.json.

1_baseline_and_stations.method: Station lines: for each row y=3200..3575 (every 3 px), took the brightest column within ±30 px, refined it with a centroid, then fitted x(y) robustly (rms 0.23-0.63 px). Baseline: peaks found by scanning columns.

baseline.finding: There are two parallel lines about 10.5 px apart. The lower one is the centreline (CL). The upper one is the keel/sternpost/stem half-siding (HS); the waterlines end on it. HS = 10 px = 0.52 ft ≈ 1.6 cells, which matches the first body-plan point hb 1.86.
baseline.tilt: The CL slopes about -0.016 (y falls toward the bow), but the station lines are nearly vertical (dx/dy about +0.005). So the two are about 0.6° off perpendicular (drawing or paper distortion). Half-breadths were therefore measured vertically from the local CL, found again at each sample x.

1_baseline_and_stations.residual_pattern: Bowed: -0.5 at both ends and +0.4 in the middle, so there is slight nonlinearity. If anything, linear extrapolation slightly overestimates the reach at both ends.

extrapolated.vs_expected: st10 is about 1.2 cells forward of the sternpost aft edge at LWL (125.9); st0 is 0.2 cells from the cutwater at LWL (671.5)

2_half_breadth_scale.FEET_scale_bar: Found at x 3926..4297, y 3702..3727, labels at y≈3745 reading 0,2,...,20. Located 21 ticks from column-profile peaks (y 3716-3724); the end ticks are at 3926.2 and 4297.1, giving 370.9 px / 20 ft = 18.55 px/ft. Major ticks every 2 ft give 18.49 px/ft. Result: 18.52 ± 0.03 px/ft. The bar is horizontal.
2_half_breadth_scale.station_spacing: 336.06 px per 54.5 cells gives 6.17 px/cell, i.e. 18.56 px per drawing-ft at 3.0065 cells/ft. This is also horizontal.
2_half_breadth_scale.key_point: LINES-plan half-breadths run vertically on the sheet, and this sheet's vertical scale differs from its horizontal one: waterlines in the sheer and body plans are 57.6 px per 3 ft, i.e. 19.2 px/ft, not 18.5. So the scale bar and station spacing cannot set the half-breadth scale. Both conversions are given: cells_V = px*3.048/19.25 = 0.15834 cells/px (recommended); cells_H = px*3.0065/18.5 = 0.16251 cells/px.
2_half_breadth_scale.best_fit_from_body_plan_crosscheck: Ratios of body-plan hb to LINES px at stations 8 and 2 come to 0.151-0.159, mean about 0.155 cells/px, i.e. about 19.66 px per true ft. cells_V is within about 2% of this; cells_H is about 5% too wide.

3_half_breadths.method: Sub-pixel ridge tracer (Gaussian-smoothed image, perpendicular search ±1.5 px, parabolic peak), seeded from vertical scans and checked visually on the overlays. Values at stations come from the trace, or from vertical scans 6-8 px either side of the dashed station line, averaged, where the trace was missing (marked 'scan'). hb_px = y_CL(local) - y_curve. ft = px/19.25.

4_waterline_heights.body_plan: Waterlines at x 5200/5450, interpolated to the keel at x≈5290: A 1918.4, B 1976.6, C 2033.7, D 2090.0, E 2148.4, F 2206.8. All sections meet the keel side at a common point y≈2261±3, so the body plan has no drag. Keel bottom ≈2310 (48 px = 2.5 ft below the rabbet).

In the sheer plan the height above the rabbet varies along the ship because of drag; the A-rabbet distance is 19.8 ft at x 1100 and 17.8 ft at x 3300.

5_crosscheck_vs_source_lines_d11.method: Body-plan [hb, z] pts were linearly interpolated at the nominal waterline Z. Diff = LINES minus body plan, in cells.

A_Z62.9.note: A at st 8 has medium confidence

5_crosscheck_vs_source_lines_d11.conclusion: With the vertical scale (0.15834 cells/px), LINES matches the body plan at F and runs 0.7-1.5 cells wider at E-A. With the horizontal scale (0.16251) it is 1.4-2.8 cells wider, so that scale is wrong for LINES half-breadths. The leftover excess points to about 0.155 cells/px (about 19.6 px/ft) for this plan, or to slightly narrow body-plan readings.

confidence_notes: Station x positions fit within 0.5 cells (rms 0.35). Station 10 extrapolates to X 127.1 and station 0 to X 671.35, in line with the expected 126 and 672.
Waterlines A-F are identified from letter blobs next to each curve at both ends, in the same top-to-bottom order as the A-F letters in the sheer and body plans. Confidence is high.
Stern values (stations 9.5, 9, 8) and bow values (stations 1, 0.5) for A-F come from verified traces, about ±1.5 px (±0.25 cells), except where marked 'scan' or 'medium'.
The bow end x of each waterline at the half-siding is good to ±3 px. The aft lift-off x for the low waterlines (D, E, F) is ±15 px, because they run tangent to the deadwood half-siding.

The half-breadth scale is the main uncertainty, about 2-5%. Half-breadths run vertically on the sheet, and its vertical scale (19.2-19.25 px/ft from waterline spacing) differs from the horizontal scale (18.52 px/ft from the FEET bar). Both conversions are given.
Heights A-F = 18/15/12/9/6/3 ft above the keel top (Z 62.9 down to 17.1), measured in the body plan. This agrees with the earlier A = Z 63. The sheer plan shows keel drag that the body plan does not.
unverified: I could not tell RAIL from SPAR DECK among the top lines at the stern and at stations 2, 1 and 0.5. Only pixel positions and candidate identities are given.
At station 2, which of the 5 crowded top lines (y 3170.5, 3185.0, 3199.5, 3207.4, 3240.6) belongs to A-D is ambiguous. D = 3240.6 and C = 3207.4 are the likely ones.
B's aft end (≈x 715) and A at station 8 (y≈3249) rest on a single scan or first-pass trace each.
I did not trace the quarter-gallery outline or the stern ends of the top lines in detail.
The cause of the 0.6° mismatch between the CL tilt and the station lines (paper distortion or drafting) was not looked into.
The keel-top y in the body plan (2261) is good to only ±3 px, which shifts every waterline height by about ±0.15 ft.

readings.task: Drawing 11 (1927 MIT PLAN VIII) SHEER PLAN, stern and bow ends: calibration, stern outline, bow stem/cutwater/head, rail-top lines at each station. Gunports were not measured.
readings.calibration: Station lines 9..1 under the sheer plan located by column-mean brightness peaks in y 2050..2300 (subpixel centroid). The lines are not quite vertical: dx/dy = +0.0095..0.0166, mean 0.013, so the scan is rotated about 0.7 deg. I used u = x - 0.013*(y-2200) and fit work X = 0.16249533*u + 18.3504 (6.154 px/cell = 18.502 px per drawing-ft, which confirms 3.0065 cells/ft, k=0.9864). Residuals against the known body-plan station X: st9 +0.03, st8 -0.01, st7 -0.02, st6 +0.01, st5 -0.03, st4 -0.01, st3 +0.07, st2 -0.02, st1 -0.01 cells. Re-checks: the sternpost aft edge at the LWL comes out at X 126.0 (known 125.9). The outer cutwater at the LWL comes out at X 671.0 (known 671.5). Vertical scale: 6 waterlines are 57.4..57.9 px apart (3 ft), so 19.22 px/ft = 0.15859 cells/px. Z datum: the keel bottom is drawn as a double line (two lines about 8 px apart, i.e. about 1.3 cells). I took Z=0 at the LOWER line (taken as the bottom of the keel shoe), fitted as y = -0.02644*x + 2414.74 (54 columns x 760..3650, rms 1.0 px). Z is measured up the station-line direction from that keel line: Z = (y_keel - y)*0.15859, so drag is built in, as plan.json asks. A separate upper keel line (top of keel / rabbet?) sits at Z 6.1 aft to 6.9 forward. That is below the work's keel top of Z 8, so drawing 11 and the work disagree by about 1.5 cells there. LWL (top waterline, y = -0.01069*x + 1977.59, rms 2.5 px): Z 67.7 at X 126, falling to 59.3 at X 671; about Z 62.7 at midships (X 449), against the stated mean 20'9" = 63.2. Drag works out to about 0.89 deg, deeper aft, which matches plan.json's 0.85 deg.

transform.keel_bottom_px: y = -0.02644*x + 2414.74 (lower line of the double keel line)
